fun_fact: Aug 17 was World Pedestrian Day — a good moment to ask how walkable Indian cities really are. Walking accounts for more than 60% of trips in urban India, yet most cities are hostile to people on foot. Decades of car-centric planning have resulted in cities that move cars and not people, and climate change makes it worse — extreme heatwaves and monsoon flooding hit pedestrians hardest. The way out isn't complicated: shaded, tree-lined streets with even footpaths, safe crossings and lighting. [Know more →](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2k_7wrxyRqI&t=11s)
author: Ishwarya
